title: Client signal draining and adaptive timeout heuristics for in-flight generations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

We observe a class of incidents where clients disconnect or stall mid-generation causing GPU resources and KV cache slots to remain allocated for long-running, partially generated sequences. These stale in-flight generations increase memory pressure, reduce throughput for other customers, and complicate billing reconciliation for partial token outputs. Existing mechanisms (fixed hard timeouts and periodic sweeps) are either too aggressive (dropping legitimate slow clients) or too lax (leaving stale generations for minutes).

Goals:
- Introduce an explicit client-drain/signal protocol to allow timely server-side cleanup when a client indicates it is aborting or wants transfer of partial output.
- Implement adaptive timeout heuristics that combine per-session pacing, recent LRU generation duration stats, and explicit client signals to determine soft vs hard eviction boundaries.
- Maintain strong customer safety: avoid throwing away valid short-lived generations; surface partial artifacts for billing and debug; ensure SLOs for other tenants are preserved.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Client-side signal extension: small, optional control message 'drain:partial' that clients can send when they are about to disconnect or request best-effort delivery of current prefix. Server reacts by marking the generation as 'draining' and triggers a fast-path flush if possible. This is backward-compatible: absent the signal, we use heuristics.

2) Soft/hard timeouts: replace single hard timeout with two thresholds per-model and per-workload: a soft timeout (e.g., 30s median * multiplier) that will start graceful eviction and attempt delivery via alternative transports (storage checkpoint / slow callback) and a hard timeout (e.g., soft + 2x) that forcibly reclaims resources. Thresholds are adaptive based on recent percentiles for the route and the current queue length.

3) Per-generation checkpointing: when a generation crosses the soft threshold or receives a 'drain' signal, persist a lightweight prefix checkpoint to our fast object store (KV metadata + last token indices) so that later resumption or post-mortem inspection is possible without keeping GPU state pinned. Checkpointing should be fast (sub-100ms) and optional for very short generations to avoid overhead.

4) Admission and preemption policy: under memory pressure, use a scored eviction policy that prefers reclaiming: (a) disconnected/draining sessions, (b) generations beyond soft timeout, (c) low-priority customers, (d) oldest inactive sessions. Avoid preempting active, streaming clients below their soft timeout.

5) Observability and billing signals: expose events for drain/start/checkpoint/reclaim with token counts, duration, and whether a generation was served to completion. Hook these into Console (per-route timeline) and billing pipeline so customers can see partial output reconciliations.

Trade-offs considered:
- Checkpointing overhead vs GPU retention: extra small write latency in exchange for freeing GPU state. Mitigate by making checkpointing opt-in and bounded to prefix size and frequency.
- Client signal adoption vs heuristic safety: rely on heuristics for non-adopting clients. Backwards compatibility preserved.
- Complexity of adaptive thresholds vs stability: start with conservative percentile-based multipliers and tune with canary traffic.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- 60% reduction in average time-to-reclaim for disconnected sessions in canary cluster within 2 weeks of rollout.
- No more than 2% increase in tail latency (p95/p99 generation latency) for active streaming clients.
- Checkpoint storage cost increases < 5% for typical workloads in experiment cohort.
- Console shows drain/reclaim events for all test routes and billing reconciliation shows partial generation entries for >= 95% of checkpointed truncations.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Phase 0 (design & spec): finalize protocol message format and checkpoint schema (owner: Aisha). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Draining+Protocol+Spec
- Phase 1 (server): implement drain flag handling, generation state transitions, adaptive timeout framework and eviction scorer. Add unit tests and simulation harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3189 (WIP) (owner: Marco).
- Phase 2 (client SDKs): add optional 'drain' control API to Node/Python streaming SDKs and backwards-compatible fallbacks. (owner: Priya Shah).
- Phase 3 (checkpointing): integrate lightweight prefix checkpoint writes and fast restore path; add retention TTL & GC. (owner: Yun Li).
- Phase 4 (canary + metrics): run canary on dedicated pool, gather SLO telemetry, iterate thresholds, and prepare rollout. (owner: Reliability team).

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Checkpoint format: full KV cache vs token-only prefix. Perf tests needed to quantify restore latency.
- Billing semantics: how to invoice for checkpointed-but-not-delivered tokens; legal/finance to advise.
- Client SDK ergonomics: how to surface 'drain' without breaking higher-level streaming abstractions.
comments: 2026-02-27 - Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and proposed approach posted. Shared spec link with runtime and SDK owners. Asked for perf budget targets for checkpoint writes.

2026-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented server-side state transitions and basic adaptive timeout window. Running local simulations; preliminary numbers show 45% faster reclamation for synthetic disconnects. PR created (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3189
2026-03-06 - Priya Shah: Drafted SDK API ergonomics. Proposing optional StreamController.drain({reason}) call. Will implement Node + Python canaries.

2026-03-09 - Reliability team (note): Need a conservative default for soft timeout multiplier to avoid evicting slow mobile clients. Suggested initial multiplier = 2x median route latency, tune via canary.

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Added eviction scorer that accounts for connection status, soft timeout overshoot, and tenant priority. Benchmarked scorer with ten simulated tenants; results attached in confluence note. Moving to integration tests this week.
notes_for_reviewers: Key places to review: adaptive timeout formula in runtime/scheduling/timeout_policy.go, checkpoint schema under storage/checkpoints, and SDK drain API ergonomics. Pay special attention to GC TTL defaults and cost/accounting impacts.
next_actions: Finish unit tests for eviction scorer, land PR for server handling behind feature flag, add SDK drain call in Node SDK, and start canary run on dedicated-dev cluster.
release_notes_draft: Add optional client 'drain' signal and adaptive timeouts for streaming sessions. Improves reclamation of disconnected generations and reduces resource contention under high churn. Checkpointing of partial generations is introduced as an opt-in feature.
